anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Row-count, histogram, density, or correlation metadata no longer matches the real data distribution, so the optimizer bases plan costing on inaccurate cardinality estimates.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database host CPUs are persistently saturated, creating a compute bottleneck that slows both query execution and supporting background tasks.

When both root causes are active, the database exhibits a blend of tell-tale symptoms: execution plans show extreme under- or over-estimates alongside very high per-statement and system-wide CPU time; run-queue and OS load averages spike during and immediately after plan compilations; statement latency and variance rise sharply even for previously fast queries; automatic statistics jobs, parallel execution crews, and user queries all contend for CPU, causing statistics refreshes to miss maintenance windows and reinforcing stale metadata; retry storms or connection pool timeouts may appear as response times lengthen.

Causal chain: stale or missing statistics mislead the optimizer into choosing CPU-heavy access paths such as wide nested loops, full scans, or over-parallelized plans. These plans drive sustained CPU demand that saturates cores, raising compile and execution times and monopolizing scheduler resources. The resulting CPU pressure delays or cancels automatic statistics collection and hinders manual refresh attempts, so statistics remain stale and misestimation persists. The two anomalies thus reinforce one another in a feedback loop that degrades throughput and increases latency across the entire workload.

entry.official_definition: The number of seconds that the mysqld server waits for a connect packet before responding with Bad handshake.
entry.trigger_condition: A client does not complete the initial connection packet exchange within connect_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The connection attempt fails during handshake.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL server system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when connection establishment, authentication exchange, or session activity does not progress within the allowed time budget.
entry.solution_guidance: Check connection lifecycle, client responsiveness, authentication latency, idle-session handling, and whether connection pools are holding stale sessions.
